# Saved-look import worth review

**A — exactly one separate complete implementation/validation/UI method proposal is worth doing. No code, test, browser action or import execution is admitted here.**

**F1 — a nondisruptive one-look collection ingress is a distinct useful consumer.** Current `showcase.js:162–169` exports one saved configuration. `openLook():316–335` reads a selected file through `readShowcaseSettings` and deliberately navigates with `location.assign`; the file chooser invokes it at487–489. The local-save form adds `currentConfiguration()` at397–403. Thus Open JSON then Save is a working consumer, but it changes the active preview before the person can keep the imported recipe.

The other selected ingress has different semantics: `showcase-collection-backup.mjs:24–34` expects the collection envelope, and71–88 previews/replaces its whole raw value. Backup UI80–102 explicitly warns that all current saved looks will be replaced, then restores. It does not provide a single-configuration append. The whole saved-export receipt, especially lines3/31, establishes actual historical portable-file download/reopening without supplying this proposed nondisruptive collection addition. Saved roadmap rows5/44 and current checklist's supported save/export features establish a concrete consumer, not an invented rendering defect.

Two alternatives: prepare one explicit single-recipe import-to-collection contract, gaining portability without preview interruption or unrelated-entry replacement, at the cost of new naming/file-read/validation/persistence/UI ownership; or retain Open JSON→Save plus whole-collection backup/restore, avoiding new ingress code/UI but requiring preview interruption for one recipe or whole replacement for a backup. The narrow optional consumer justifies the former proposal.

**The existing owners are interfaces, not qualified safety proof.** Host imports at5/7 and calls at322/401 witness a reader and collection-add path; this review did not inspect those implementations.
